Presented at the UN Forum on Business and Human Rights in Geneva, the Pode Contar mechanism combines listening to rural workers, social dialogue and strategic information to support companies in preventing labour and human rights risks and in providing access to remedy in supply chains.

SÃO PAULO, Brazil--(BUSINESS WIRE)--How can companies identify labour risks that do not always surface in traditional compliance checks, and act before problems escalate? That is the aim of Pode Contar, a mechanism presented on Monday (23 November) at “The World of Work in Transformation”, an event held alongside the 15th United Nations Forum on Business and Human Rights in Geneva, Switzerland.

Developed by the International Labour Organization (ILO) and Brazil’s National Confederation of Rural Wage Workers (CONTAR), in strategic partnership with the UN Global Compact Network Brazil and Suzano, Pode Contar seeks to turn workers’ day-to-day experience into an opportunity for prevention, dialogue and improved working conditions in rural supply chains.

The initiative is built on three complementary pillars: structured listening to workers, dialogue to address and resolve problems, and the generation of strategic information to identify and prevent risks.

By telephone or WhatsApp, via text or voice message, rural workers can ask questions, seek guidance and report concerns about their working conditions, free of charge and confidentially. The service is provided by CONTAR, which is responsible for receiving and handling requests in accordance with established protocols.

From listening to prevention and remedy

Pode Contar seeks to identify problems at an early stage and create opportunities for solutions through social dialogue. Where appropriate, reported situations may be discussed with the employer, allowing for clarification, the adoption of corrective measures and remedy for impacts on workers.

Reports submitted by workers are handled according to their nature, distinguishing between questions, concerns, unverified allegations and confirmed situations. The mechanism does not replace labour inspection. Cases requiring action by the competent authorities, such as situations indicating a risk to workers’ lives or physical safety, follow specific protocols.

“People who work in rural areas need to know where to turn when they have questions about their rights or face a problem at work. Through Pode Contar, workers can contact CONTAR directly and confidentially to receive guidance and support in finding a solution. We also visit worksites and communities to talk about rights and explain how to seek remedy in case of violations. Social dialogue is part of this work: through it, workers take part, alongside employers and public institutions, in building solutions to remedy violations and prevent them from recurring,” explained Laissa Pollyana Carmo, Project Coordinator at CONTAR.

Intelligence for corporate due diligence

Beyond individual follow-up, Pode Contar makes it possible to turn information gathered from workers into analyses of recurring labour and occupational safety and health risks in supply chains. Aggregated and anonymized data help reveal patterns related to recruitment, working hours, pay, safety and health, transport and accommodation, including situations that are not easily identified in periodic audits.

For companies, producers and other supply chain actors, this information can function as a complementary early warning and response system, supporting risk identification, priority setting and the monitoring of preventive and corrective measures. The analyses can inform collective initiatives and dialogue forums, in compliance with confidentiality and data protection rules.

“What sets Pode Contar apart is that it connects workers’ voices to the response capacity of companies and institutions. By combining listening, social dialogue and strategic information, the mechanism helps identify risks at an early stage, prevent violations and strengthen access to remedy. It is an approach that recognizes the role of workers, employers and public institutions in building solutions to promote decent work,” said Maria Cláudia Falcão, Coordinator of the Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work Programme at the ILO Country Office for Brazil.

Pode Contar’s approach is aligned with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and with ILO frameworks on grievance mechanisms and access to remedy. It also contributes to corporate due diligence processes in line with the OECD Guidelines and the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD).

“No company can tackle human rights challenges in rural supply chains alone. Pode Contar was born of this conviction: by bringing companies, workers and institutions together through a listening channel facilitated by CONTAR, it reaches people who might not otherwise use a company-level grievance mechanism. For companies, this means seeing risks that audits do not always capture, prioritizing actions based on evidence and demonstrating, in practice, their commitment to decent work. The initiative already reaches the forestry and coffee sectors and has great potential to inspire other supply chains,” said Gabriela Rozman, Senior Manager for Human Rights and Labour at the UN Global Compact Network Brazil.

Grounded in the ILO principles of social dialogue and tripartism, Pode Contar recognizes the importance of involving workers, employers and public institutions. Although operated by CONTAR, the mechanism provides for dialogue with companies and institutional coordination, complementing company grievance channels and public instruments for protecting labour rights.

Implementation in rural supply chains

In addition to the service channel, Pode Contar offers training on decent work. The mechanism was designed for people who work in the field, with no need to travel to an office or use a computer. In the forestry sector, implementation began in Espírito Santo and will expand to other locations in 2027 and may later be extended to other rural supply chains.

Suzano, the world’s largest pulp producer and a global benchmark in manufacturing eucalyptus-based bioproducts, is responsible for bringing the channel to the forestry sector and its own value chain. The initiative builds on the partnership established in 2024 between Suzano, the ILO and the UN Global Compact to strengthen human rights due diligence and promote decent work throughout the chain. The company also presented the project on the main stage of the 15th United Nations Forum on Business and Human Rights.

“At Suzano, human rights are part of our strategy and of how we manage the business as a whole. Pode Contar puts this vision into practice by incorporating the perspective of forestry workers into a structured process of human rights due diligence and value chain management. This structured listening helps us identify early warning signs, strengthen prevention and response measures and make more informed decisions, contributing to more responsible relationships and business resilience,” said Giordano Automare, Executive Sustainability Manager at Suzano. “That is why the more companies join Pode Contar, the greater our capacity to work with partners to strengthen the entire chain, prevent risks and create shared value for workers and the business, placing people and sustainability at the centre of decision-making,” he added.

In addition to forestry, Pode Contar is being implemented in the coffee and carnauba sectors, through local mobilization and engagement with workers, companies and partner institutions. Experience in these sectors may guide improvements to the mechanism and its expansion to other rural supply chains.

How to access Pode Contar

The service is free of charge and available by telephone and WhatsApp: 0800 100 4044. Pode Contar is also on Instagram (@podecontarbr) and LinkedIn (https://www.linkedin.com/company/podecontarbr/).

Key Terms

occupational safety and healthtechnical
Occupational safety and health is the field concerned with preventing work-related injuries and illnesses and protecting workers’ physical and mental well-being. It includes identifying workplace hazards and using measures such as safer equipment, procedures, training, and protective gear to reduce risks.
grievance mechanismsregulatory
A grievance mechanism is a formal process a company provides for workers, customers, local communities or suppliers to report harms, complaints or rule violations and seek investigation or remedy. It matters to investors because effective mechanisms act like a safety valve—catching and fixing small problems before they escalate into costly lawsuits, supply disruptions or reputation damage—and they signal better management, transparency and lower long‑term risk.
tripartismtechnical
Tripartism is a system of consultation or decision-making involving three groups, most commonly government, employers and workers or their representatives. In labor and employment policy, it gives each group a role in discussing or shaping rules and agreements.

  • Schneider Electric is increasing Cooling Distribution Unit (CDU) manufacturing capacity by 100% at its Conselve facility in Italy, with expanded production capacity expected from January 2027
  • Chiller manufacturing capacity will increase by 50% by the end of 2026, supporting growing demand for AI and high-density data center cooling across Europe
  • A new advanced cooling test laboratory will triple existing testing capacity by December 2027, strengthening Schneider Electric’s European leadership in cooling innovation, R&D and product validation

CONSELVE, Italy, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Schneider Electric, a global energy technology leader, has today announced a major expansion of its European cooling manufacturing capabilities at its Conselve facility in Italy, doubling production capacity for advanced liquid cooling technologies to support the rapid growth of AI and high-density data centers across Europe.

The expansion, which follows the acquisition of Motivair last year, will increase CDU manufacturing capacity by 100% from January 2027, alongside a 50% increase in Big Chiller manufacturing capacity by the end of 2026. The development strengthens Schneider Electric's European industrial footprint, industrializing its advanced cooling manufacturing capabilities, and bringing both engineering and technical expertise closer to customers while supporting the deployment of AI-ready digital infrastructure.

As part of this expansion, Schneider Electric is investing in a new advanced cooling test laboratory, targeted for completion in December 2027. The facility will triple existing testing capacity, strengthening R&D, product validation and quality assurance for next-generation air and liquid cooling technologies. This investment further accelerates innovation by providing advanced validation capabilities for chillers up to 4 MW, Motivair by Schneider Electric CDUs up to 5 MW and CRAH and fan wall systems up to 800 kW.

Located in the Veneto region of Italy, Conselve remains Schneider Electric's largest cooling manufacturing facility in Europe and a central hub for research and development, engineering and technical training.

"AI is fundamentally transforming the way in which our customers design and operate data centers, creating unprecedented demand for advanced liquid cooling technologies that can support increasingly powerful computing systems," said Damien Dhellemmes, senior vice president of the Secure Power and Data Center Business in Europe at Schneider Electric. "By doubling our liquid cooling manufacturing capacity in Conselve, we're strengthening our ability to deploy resilient, scalable and energy-efficient AI infrastructure, while bringing critical technologies and expertise closer to our customers in Europe."

Accelerating European cooling innovation

As AI workloads drive higher rack densities and increasingly complex thermal requirements, liquid cooling is becoming essential to the next generation of data center infrastructure. Schneider Electric's expansion at Conselve will strengthen its ability to meet these demands through increased manufacturing capacity, greater supply-chain resilience and closer collaboration with European customers.

The development also complements Schneider Electric's broader liquid cooling portfolio, including Motivair by Schneider Electric, combining specialist cooling expertise with the company's end-to-end capabilities across power, cooling, software and services.

Investing in Europe's industrial future

The expansion reflects Schneider Electric's continued investment in European manufacturing and specialist technical skills. Over the past five years, Conselve's workforce has nearly doubled, supporting growth across engineering, production, quality assurance and technical functions.

Through its expanded manufacturing and innovation capabilities, Schneider Electric is reinforcing its commitment to delivering the resilient, efficient and scalable infrastructure needed to support Europe's rapidly growing digital economy.

VANCOUVER, BC AND BREDA, THE NETHERLANDS / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Organto Foods Inc. (TSXV:OGO)(OTCQX:OGOFF)(FSE:OGF0) ("Organto" or "the Company"), is pleased to announce its financial results for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. All amounts are expressed in Canadian dollars and in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), except where specifically noted.

"Q-3 2026 was another record quarter for our Company. Our third quarter sales grew 67% to $25.2 million, the largest third quarter sales in the history of the Company, while gross profit, adjusted gross profit (1) and adjusted EBITDA (1) also reached third quarter records. Equally important, our balance sheet remains strong with $14.5 million of working capital, no long-term debt and net equity of $15.6 million. Following our business repositioning through 2024 and early 2025, our goal was to continue to expand our commercial and operating base, while positioning to achieve positive adjusted EBITDA (1) in 2026. We have realized these objectives and in fact this quarter represents our third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA (1) results, demonstrating the strength and adaptability of our scalable, capital-efficient ecosystem. These results reinforce our confidence in the opportunities that lie ahead as we continue to build a world-class organic and fairtrade foods company." commented Steve Bromley, Co-Chair and Chief Executive Officer.

Key Highlights

  • Sales increased 67% to a third quarter record of $25.2 million. Largest third quarter sales in Company's history.
  • Adjusted gross profit (1) when accounting for the impact of currency hedging related to gross profit increased to $2.1 million or 8.2% of sales, an increase of 206% versus the prior year. Largest third quarter gross profit and adjusted gross profit (1) dollars in the Company's history.
  • Cash overhead expenses (1) decreased to 7.8% of sales versus 8.9% in the prior year, demonstrating continued operating leverage.
  • Adjusted EBITDA (1) improved to $0.3 million from a loss of $0.7 million in the prior year. Largest third quarter adjusted EBITDA (1) in the Company's history.
  • Annualized sales run rate (2) continues in excess of $100 million.
  • Working capital increased to $14.5 million.
  • No long-term debt outstanding.
  • Cash balance remained strong at $7.9 million.
  • Equity of $15.6 million, up 78% versus December 31, 2025

Steve Bromley further commented, "We remain focused and committed to building a world-class organic and fairtrade foods company serving growing global healthy and sustainable foods markets, with the goal of creating long-term value for our operating partners, customers, team members and shareholders. We continue to gain momentum in our business and believe our third quarter results reflect another important point in our journey. At the same time, we are working to expand our geographic footprint and product mix with the goal of increasing our market presence and operating margins through increased value-add."

  • Mr. He Xiaopeng, Chairman & CEO of XPENG, outlines the technological breakthroughs needed to bring humanoid robots into mass production, positioning physical AI as the next frontier of technological innovation.

GUANGZHOU, China, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Chairman & CEO of XPeng Inc. (“XPENG” or the “Company,” NYSE: XPEV; HKEX: 9868), a leading global Physical AI company, has contributed an article titled "Get Ready for Humanoid Robots"to The Economist's The World Ahead 2027, sharing his perspectives on the development of humanoid robots and the future of artificial intelligence in the physical world.

Published on November 18, 2026, the article explores the technological challenges and opportunities shaping the humanoid robotics industry, offering insights into how advanced general-purpose of humanoid robots could move beyond demonstrations and enter real-world applications.

Mr. He Xiaopeng emphasizes the importance of an integrated approach to humanoid robotics, stating: "Robots must be designed with a software mindset, but hardware must come first. Robots also need multiple speeds of thought, and the data they learn from needs variety, not merely volume." This philosophy highlights the need to develop hardware, software and data capabilities in tandem, building a comprehensive technological foundation that enables robots to perceive, reason, move and interact reliably in complex real-world environments. This full-stack approach is essential to accelerating the deployment and commercialization of humanoid robots.


XPENG's advanced general-purpose of humanoid robot IRON

Rethinking Intelligence: Humanoid Robots Need Multiple Speeds of Thought

One of the key insights into Mr. He Xiaopeng's article is that humanoid robots require fundamentally different layers of intelligence to operate effectively in the physical world.

"Rather than one all-purpose brain, humanoid robots will need several speeds of thought: ultra-fast models for motor control and split-second reflexes; fast models for motion and real-time interaction; slow models for reasoning and memory; separate models dedicated to safety." This vision is reflected in XPENG's Turing Physical AI Architecture (VLA 3.0), unveiled at XPENG AI Day 2026.

Designed to connect intelligence with physical execution, the architecture integrates three systems operating at different levels and speeds:

  • System 0 – Ultra-fast System: Integrates physical control into the AI loop, coordinating hardware, power, communication and execution while ensuring real-time body-state feedback and safe operation.
  • System 1 – Fast System: Powered by XPENG's VLA 2.0, enables real-time environmental perception and translates understanding into rapid, executable actions.
  • System 2 – Slow System: Combines vision-language-based task planning with an Agent Runtime state machine to support higher-level reasoning, complex task planning and coordinated decision-making.

Together, the three systems form a unified, continuous closed loop connecting cognition, action and physical feedback, enabling humanoid robots to think, respond and interact safely with the real world.

However, for general-purpose humanoid robots, progress is still needed in four areas: learning to move safely , handling tools and navigating different environments, acquiring and applying specialist knowledge and skills, and developing social and emotional intelligence to act appropriately in different situations.

2027: A New Milestone for Humanoid Robot Commercialization

In his contribution to The Economist, Mr. He Xiaopeng points to 2027 as a significant milestone for the humanoid robotics industry, anticipating the beginning of mass production of advanced general-purpose of humanoid robots. It will require not only advances in AI intelligence and mechanical capabilities, but also improvements in manufacturing efficiency, reliability, safety and cost competitiveness.


XPENG IRON

XPENG believes commercialization will progress in stages, starting with more structured commercial applications. XPENG’s humanoid robot IRON is designed to serve as a work partner and is scheduled to begin training as a store assistant at XPENG retail stores in Q1 2027. "First in commercial settings, then in industrial applications and, ultimately, in the home. " This gradual approach will allow humanoid robots to accumulate real-world experience, improve their capabilities and build the reliability required for broader adoption.

Building on its expertise in intelligent mobility, autonomous driving and robotics, XPENG is committed to advancing physical AI and turning technological breakthroughs into real-world applications.

("Saxony"), a majority-owned subsidiary of Excellon, all as more particularly described in the Circular.

The board of directors of Excellon (the "Excellon Board") has unanimously determined that the transactions contemplated by the Arrangement are fair to Excellon Shareholders and are in the best interests of Excellon and the Excellon Shareholders. Accordingly, the Excellon Board has unanimously approved the Arrangement and unanimously recommends that Excellon Shareholders vote FOR the Arrangement Resolution. In accordance with the interim order granted by the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) on November 16, 2026, providing for the calling and holding of the Meeting and other procedural matters relating to the Arrangement, the Arrangement can only proceed if, among other conditions, it receives the approval of not less than two-thirds (66⅔%) of the votes cast on the Arrangement Resolution by Excellon Shareholders in person (virtually) or by proxy at the Meeting.

Excellon Shareholders will retain their proportionate ownership in Excellon.

As a result of, and immediately following the completion of, the Arrangement, the Excellon Shareholders will directly own approximately 48.0% of the Saxony Shares and Excellon will retain approximately 19.9% of the Saxony Shares, in each case on an undiluted basis.

Saxony has applied to list the Saxony Shares on the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV"). At the Meeting, Excellon Shareholders will be asked to consider and, if deemed advisable, pass a special resolution authorizing an amendment to the articles of the Company to effect the Proposed Change of Name. FRAMINGHAM, Mass. & SALISBURY, England--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Please replace the KalVista U.S. website listed in the sentence above the reference section with the KalVista U.K. website (www.kalvista.co.uk) in the release dated November 25, 2026.

The updated release reads:

NICE RECOMMENDS EKTERLY®▼ (SEBETRALSTAT) THE FIRST ORAL, ON-DEMAND TREATMENT OPTION FOR HEREDITARY ANGIOEDEMA (HAE) ATTACKS

The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has issued final draft guidance recommending sebetralstat, within its marketing authorisation, as an oral, on-demand option for the treatment of HAE attacks in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older on the National Health Service (NHS) in England and Wales.

KalVista Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (“KalVista”), a company of the Chiesi Group, welcomed a decision by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) to recommend sebetralstat, within its marketing authorisation, as an oral option for the on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema (HAE) attacks in adult and adolescent patients aged 12 years and older on the National Health Service (NHS) in England and Wales.1

HAE is a rare genetic disease that causes unpredictable, painful attacks of tissue swelling in various locations of the body that can be life-threatening depending on the area affected.2 It is estimated to affect 1,000 to 1,500 people across the United Kingdom.3 Sebetralstat works by blocking plasma kallikrein, which is a protein that plays a key role in swelling in HAE attacks.4

The recommendation is informed by results from the phase 3 KONFIDENT clinical trial, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-way cross-over design, published in the New England Journal of Medicine.5

Across the study, 110 patients treated a total of 264 attacks. These included 87 attacks treated with sebetralstat 300 mg and 84 treated with placebo. Attacks ranged in severity from mild to very severe and occurred in all anatomical locations.4 An additional dose could be taken if needed following initial treatment of an attack. The primary efficacy endpoint was the time to beginning of symptom relief, assessed using the Patient Reported Global Impression of Change (PGI-C), which required patients to assess their attack symptoms using a seven-point scale (“much worse” to “much better”). To achieve the primary endpoint, a patient had to report a positive and sustained response on the PGI-C within 12 hours. There was a statistically significant faster time to the beginning of symptom relief for 300 mg sebetralstat (Bonferroni adjusted p<0.0001) compared to placebo. The median time to the beginning of symptom relief was 1.61 hours (95% CI: 1.28 - 2.27) with sebetralstat 300 mg, compared with 6.72 hours (95% CI: 2.33 - NE) with placebo (NE = not evaluable at 12 hours).

In clinical studies used for registration, 1,945 HAE attacks have been treated with sebetralstat. The most common adverse reaction in HAE patients treated with sebetralstat is headache (reported by 9.2% of patients). The reported events of headache were generally mild to moderate in severity, non-serious and resolved without any further intervention.

About Hereditary Angioedema (HAE)
Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is a rare genetic disease resulting in deficiency or dysfunction in the C1 esterase inhibitor (C1INH) protein and subsequent uncontrolled activation of the kallikrein-kinin system.3 People living with HAE experience painful and debilitating attacks of tissue swelling in various locations of the body that can be life-threatening depending on the area affected.2 Treatment guidelines recommend treating attacks as early as possible to prevent progression of swelling and shorten the time to attack resolution, and to consider treatment for all attacks, regardless of anatomic location or severity.6,7

About EKTERLY® (sebetralstat)
EKTERLY (sebetralstat) is a competitive, reversible inhibitor of plasma kallikrein and is indicated for the treatment of hereditary angioedema (HAE) attacks in adult and adolescents aged 12 years and older.

For complete product information, please see the Summary of Product Characteristics that can be found on https://products.mhra.gov.uk/.

About KalVista Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
KalVista, a company of the Chiesi Group, is a global pharmaceutical company dedicated to delivering oral therapies for people affected by rare diseases with significant unmet needs. The KalVista team discovered and developed sebetralstat for hereditary angioedema (HAE) and continues to work closely with the global HAE community to improve treatment and care worldwide. As part of Chiesi Global Rare Diseases, a Chiesi Group business unit established to deliver innovative therapies and solutions for people living with rare diseases, KalVista is building on its expertise in HAE and contributing to a shared mission to help underserved rare disease communities live their most fulfilling lives.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - BrandPilot AI Inc. (CSE: BPAI) (OTCQB: BPAIF) (FSE: 8LH0) ("BrandPilot" or the "Company"), a performance marketing technology company, today announced the commercial availability of BrandPilot Analytics, a digital analytics offering, designed to help businesses understand website activity and provide actionable intelligence as the web enters a new era of automated and agentic interaction.

BrandPilot Analytics helps businesses measure website activity, understand visitor behaviour, track marketing campaigns and assess traffic quality in a centralized reporting environment. The offering combines unsampled reporting with privacy-focused measurement and visibility into indicators of automated and agentic website activity.

"The rise of agentic AI is changing how people discover information, evaluate products and interact with businesses online," said Brandon Mina, Chief Executive Officer of BrandPilot AI. "Marketers need to understand not just who visits their websites, but what automated and agentic systems are doing there, how they interact with digital properties and what that activity means for marketing performance. BrandPilot Analytics is our response to this shift, giving businesses greater visibility into the traffic reaching their digital properties and the behaviour taking place there."

Analytics and Measurement Capabilities

As AI agents increasingly browse, compare, navigate and take actions on behalf of people, website traffic can no longer be understood through human-visitor metrics alone. Cloudflare, a global web infrastructure company that sits between users and websites and powers about 45% of the Fortune 500, reported in September 2026 that, for the first time, more than half of internet traffic observed across its network was non-human. Furthermore, daily requests from AI agents on its network had grown by more than 1,700% over the preceding year.[1] HUMAN Security reported that traffic from AI agents and agentic browsers grew 7,851% year over year in 2025.[2] While these figures come from different datasets and methodologies, and should not be treated as directly comparable; together, they clearly indicate that automated and agentic activity is becoming an increasingly important part of the online environment. This proliferation in automation and agentic traffic brings with it a new layer of complexity for marketeers, as the signals they historically relied on, no longer provide accurate insights.

BrandPilot Analytics brings together four areas of measurement capability:

  • Analytics and reporting: Website traffic, visitor geography, devices, browsers, acquisition sources, audience segmentation, custom dashboards and reporting based on the collected dataset without statistical sampling.
  • Traffic quality: Visibility into indicators of automated, bot and AI-agent activity to help businesses understand the composition of incoming website traffic and distinguish agentic interactions from conventional human visits.
  • Campaign and conversion measurement: Campaign tracking, goals, conversion reporting, e-commerce analytics and measurement across acquisition channels.
  • Behavioural analytics and optimization: Heatmaps, session recordings, user flows, conversion funnels, form analytics and A/B testing to help analyze visitor journeys and potential improvements to website performance.

The offering is designed to minimize personal data collection and avoid collecting personally identifiable information (PII), subject to the product's implementation and configuration.

Building Toward a More Unified Marketing Performance Platform

BrandPilot Analytics expands the Company's portfolio alongside AdAi, ClickRadar™ and SearchIQ™. The Company intends to progressively connect capabilities spanning digital analytics, paid search efficiency, invalid traffic identification and brand visibility across generative AI search platforms, with the longer-term objective of giving marketers a more integrated view of human, automated and agentic activity and its impact on marketing performance.

"Marketers often rely on multiple tools to understand different parts of their digital performance," said Seif Kheimaisia, Chief Growth Officer of BrandPilot AI. "Our strategy is to progressively bring more of that intelligence together. BrandPilot Analytics adds an important measurement capability to the portfolio and supports our broader objective of connecting analytics with traffic quality, advertising efficiency and media accountability. The new analytics offering broadens brands' capabilities to generate actionable intelligence and optimize campaigns accordingly, a major need we identified among our clients."

BrandPilot Analytics is commercially available. The Company intends to pursue adoption through its existing enterprise relationships, agency partnerships and broader business development activities.

About BrandPilot AI

BrandPilot AI (CSE: BPAI) is a performance marketing technology company headquartered in Toronto, focused on identifying and eliminating inefficiencies in digital advertising for global enterprise brands. The Company's core capabilities include AdAi, which eliminates cannibalistic branded search spend that inflates costs without driving incremental value; ClickRadar™, which compiles forensic bot-detection reports to reclaim refunds associated with invalid traffic; and SearchIQ™, which enables brands to measure and optimize their presence across generative AI search platforms.

BrandPilot is purpose-built to address structural challenges in modern digital advertising, where increasing automation and scale can reduce transparency and accountability. Operating as an independent performance and validation layer, the Company helps enterprises recover wasted budgets, restore data integrity, and gain clearer visibility into how advertising dollars are spent so performance can be improved with greater confidence

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / SILVER X MINING CORP. (TSXV:AGX)(OTCQX:AGXPF)(F:AGX) ("Silver X" or the "Company"), a growing silver producer building a multi-asset precious metals platform in Peru, reports its financial and operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and provides an update on the expansion of its operation, including the Recuperada processing plant.

Silver X generated third quarter net operating revenue of $10.1M and operating income of $1.4M, both higher than a year earlier, while reporting a net loss of $1.7M. 3Q26 was a transition quarter focused on the expansion of the Recuperada processing plant to 1,000 tpd. Throughput and sales volumes declined sequentially as plant expansion activities constrained processing rates and the Tangana mine prioritized underground development to open the production faces required to support higher throughput.

Mechanical issues with equipment installed for the expansion subsequently delayed the Recuperada ramp-up beyond the previously disclosed schedule. Management is prioritizing improving metallurgical recoveries while completing the remaining expansion works and currently expects sustained throughput of 1,000 tonnes per day ("tpd") in 1Q27.

"We have a clear set of operating priorities: complete the Recuperada expansion, get metallurgical recoveries back to where they should be and establish sustained throughput at 1,000 tonnes per day," said José M. Garcia, CEO of Silver X. "The ramp-up has taken longer than planned, and we are addressing the equipment and processing issues directly. With additional mining faces opened at Tangana and financial flexibility to support the remaining work, we are focused on completing the expansion with discipline.

"Our expanded resource base reinforces the scale of the opportunity at Nueva Recuperada. We are tightening operational oversight and advancing an updated Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA), with a clear focus on translating that potential into consistent operating performance and stronger cash generation."

Third Quarter and YTD Highlights

  • Net operating revenue of $10.1M, up 103% from 3Q25 and down 42% from 2Q26.
  • Operating income of $1.4M, compared with $0.5M in 3Q25 and $7.5M in 2Q26; Adjusted EBITDA of $1.0M, compared with $0.1M and $6.9M, respectively.
  • Net loss of $1.7M, compared with a net loss of $0.3M in 3Q25 and net income of $3.1M in 2Q26.
  • Ore processed of 54,681 tonnes, up 63% year-over-year and down 12% sequentially; silver-equivalent ("AgEq") production of 225,237 ounces, up 35% year-over-year and down 20% sequentially. Ore mined totaled 60,694 tonnes, approximately 6,000 tonnes above ore processed, building stockpile ahead of higher planned processing rates.
  • Nine-month net operating revenue of $40.8M and net income of $6.0M, compared with $15.6M and a net loss of $0.7M, respectively, in the prior-year period.
  • Cash of $43.3M and working capital of $26.7M at September 30, 2026, compared with cash of $10.1M and a working-capital deficit of $5.7M at December 31, 2025.

Recuperada Expansion and Operating Update

The Recuperada plant processed an average of 594 tpd during 3Q26, compared with 684 tpd in 2Q26, as expansion related repairs and installation work constrained processing rates. Tangana underground development advanced to 3,397 metres from 3,159 metres in 2Q26, opening additional production faces. A greater proportion of feed from development headings resulted in lower silver, lead, and zinc grades than in the preceding quarter.

After quarter-end, throughput averaged 598 tpd in October and 709 tpd from November 1 to 15. At October 31, 2026, the ore stockpile was approximately 12,200 tonnes. These preliminary results are subject to change and do not represent sustained operation at the targeted rate.

Metallurgical recoveries during the ramp-up have been below levels achieved earlier in 2026, particularly for lead, zinc, and gold. The Company is limiting throughput while completing the remaining expansion works and adjusting the flotation circuit. Installation is scheduled for completion in early December 2026, with recoveries to be restored before processing rates increase. Lower throughput and recoveries are expected to affect fourth quarter production and unit costs.

In November, the CEO initiated an operational and cost-reduction review covering mine planning, contractor services, staffing, equipment maintenance, procurement, third-party ore purchases, and general and administrative costs. A monthly operations committee chaired by the CEO has been established to monitor execution and operating performance. Additional tailings storage capacity is also being advanced to support higher throughput, with construction planned for 1Q27.

Financial Performance

Higher sales volumes and realized silver and zinc prices drove the year-over-year revenue increase, partially offset by a lower realized gold price. Sequentially, net operating revenue declined 42% from $17.3M in 2Q26, primarily reflecting a 27% decrease in AgEq ounces sold as expansion activities constrained throughput, together with lower average realized precious metal prices and negative provisional pricing adjustments.

The average realized silver price was $63.00 per ounce, compared with $72.67 in 2Q26, while the average realized gold price was $3,321.60 per ounce, compared with $4,505.20. The reported realized gold price was affected by negative mark-to-market adjustments on provisionally priced concentrate sales under the Company's offtake arrangements.

Cost of sales declined to $8.7M from $9.8M in 2Q26, but did not decline proportionately with revenue, reducing operating income. The quarterly net loss included $0.6M in non-cash share-based payments and $1.3M in net finance costs. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.0M, compared with $0.1M in 3Q25 and $6.9M in 2Q26.

Unit Costs and Sustaining Investment

Cash costs were $37.97 per AgEq ounce produced and all-in sustaining costs (AISC) were $49.01 per AgEq ounce, compared with $34.33 and $46.10, respectively, in 2Q26. Per tonne processed, cash costs remained steady at $156.41 from $156.10, while AISC declined to $201.87 from $209.61 compared with 2Q26.

The differing trends also reflect fewer AgEq ounces produced per tonne and changes in sustaining expenditures. Sustaining capital expenditures declined to $1.5 million from $2.6 million in 2Q26. AgEq comparisons are also affected by period metal prices: higher silver prices reduce the relative silver-equivalent contribution of lead and zinc.

Year-to-Date Results and Financial Position

Higher precious metal production and realized prices drove the year-to-date financial improvement. Operating income reached $16.0M, compared with $2.1M in the prior-year period, while Adjusted EBITDA increased to $13.8M from $0.9M.

Cash provided by operating activities was $2.4M for the nine-month period, after $11.1M was absorbed by changes in non-cash working capital. Cash used in investing activities was $18.0M, including mine development, processing and tailings infrastructure, and exploration and evaluation expenditures.

Working capital was $26.7M at September 30, 2026, compared with a deficit of $5.7M at December 31, 2025. The year-to-date improvement in liquidity primarily reflects the March 2026 secured convertible debenture financing, which generated net proceeds of $46.6M. The debentures bear interest at 10% annually.

Resource Growth and Development Plans

In October 2026, Silver X filed the technical report supporting the updated Nueva Recuperada Mineral Resource Estimate, effective August 31, 2026. The estimate includes:

  • Measured and Indicated Mineral Resources of 10.4 million tonnes grading 202 g/t AgEq, containing 67.3 million AgEq ounces, including 38.8 million ounces of silver.
  • Inferred Mineral Resources of 21.6 million tonnes grading 260 g/t AgEq, containing 184.3 million AgEq ounces, including 120.1 million ounces of silver.

Silver X continues underground development, drilling and test mining at Red Silver and is evaluating development opportunities at Blenda Rubia within the Plata Mining Unit.

An updated Preliminary Economic Assessment ("PEA"), expected in the first half of 2027, will incorporate the 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate, and evaluate a larger development scenario, including greater processing capacity and a longer mine life. Expansion of permitted capacity, including a new processing plant at Tangana, remains dependent on approval of the updated Environmental and Social Impact Assessment.

The updated PEA will replace the production profile and schedule in the 2025 PEA. Given the delay in achieving sustained throughput of 1,000 tpd and the timing of environmental approvals, the Company no longer considers 2029 a reliable date for reaching 3,000 tpd and annual production of more than six million AgEq ounces. Readers should not rely on that previously disclosed timetable.

Mineral Resources are not Mineral Reserves and do not have demonstrated economic viability. The 2025 PEA is preliminary in nature, includes Inferred Mineral Resources considered too speculative geologically to have economic considerations applied to them that would enable their categorization as Mineral Reserves, and there is no certainty that its results will be realized.

EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA

EBITDA is calculated as net income or loss before finance costs, income tax, and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA excludes share-based payments, foreign exchange gains or losses and the provision for administrative sanctions. Management believes these measures are useful indicators for investors and uses them in evaluating the Company's operating performance. Cash Costs and All-In Sustaining Cost ("AISC")
